key_insight: You can produce valid, deployment-relevant comparative safety scores for candidate language models even when no labeled benchmark exists by formalizing a controlled, scenario-based audit contract and treating scores as valid only under that fixed contract. This reframes validation from absolute ground-truth labels to reproducible, conditional evidence tied to audit choices.
problem_solved: How to compare and validate safety of language models in domains, languages, or regulatory contexts where no ground-truth labeled benchmark is available.
method: Formalize the 'benchmarkless comparative safety scoring' setting and define an explicit audit contract (scenario pack, rubric, auditor, judge, sampling configuration, rerun budget).
Use scenario-based audits and controlled experimental choices in place of labels so that comparative scores carry clear, conditional validity statements.
Provide a validation protocol and statistical controls (sampling and rerun budgets) that link observed comparative outcomes to deployment evidence under the specified contract.
impact: Enables practitioners to generate reproducible, interpretable safety comparisons and deployment evidence without waiting for labeled benchmarks, by making assumptions and audit choices explicit. This reduces uncertainty in model selection for new languages, sectors, or regulatory regimes.
visual_elements: Contract diagram showing the fixed components (scenario pack, rubric, auditor, judge, sampling config, rerun budget) and how they constrain validity
Flowchart of the scenario-based audit process from scenario sampling → model responses → judged comparisons → comparative score
Bar/rank chart comparing multiple models under the same audit contract with annotations indicating conditional validity
Checklist/icon set showing 'what must remain fixed' to preserve score validity (so practitioners know audit preconditions)
paper_title: When No Benchmark Exists: Validating Comparative LLM Safety Scoring Without Ground-Truth Labels
paper_authors: Sushant Gautam, Finn Schwall, Annika Willoch Olstad, Fernando Vallecillos Ruiz, Birk Torpmann-Hagen
